description: How many of the team's kills its Hunters helped with using their Basic abilities on the tick the enemy died. Count each enemy death once, even if several agents of this class helped. Help must come from Basic damage. Different classes can help with the same kill, so their shares can add up to more than 100%.
Extra damage the team dealt because of Mage auras. Compares the same attacks with the auras turned off, keeping Burst and enemy defenses the same. Measures overlapping auras together.
Damage the team avoided because of Warrior auras. Compares the same attacks with those auras turned off. Measures overlapping auras together.

How many of the team's kills its Mages helped with using their Basic abilities on the tick the enemy died. Count each enemy death once, even if several agents of this class helped. Help must come from Basic damage. A Mage's Basic attack during Burst counts here. Different classes can help with the same kill, so their shares can add up to more than 100%.

What share of the team's kills its Warriors helped with using their Ultimates on the kill tick. Count each enemy death once even if several agents of this class helped. Help must come from direct Ultimate damage.
How many enemies the team killed while they already had this status at the start of the tick. Each death counts once for this status, even if several teammates helped.
How many ticks Freedom let each agent move faster despite a slow. Counts even if the agent stood still. This is not distance traveled. Adds everyone's ticks on the team.
How often Freedom weakened a slow on each agent while it was alive, without a stun or spawn shield. This also depends on how much enemies slowed the agent. Adds everyone's counted ticks on the team.

How much damage the team dealt to enemies who already had this status at the start of the tick. Includes damage beyond their remaining health. Damage that breaks an existing Trap still counts. One attack can count under several statuses.

What share of the team's saves had help from Basic healing. Count each saved ally once per tick, even if several Priests helped. One save can have Basic and Ultimate help, so those shares can add up to more than 100%.
What share of the team's rescues had help from an Ultimate. This shows Ultimate use, not whether using Ultimates more often is better.

What share of the team's kills its Mages helped with using their Basic abilities on the tick the enemy died. Count each enemy death once, even if several agents of this class helped. Help must come from Basic damage. A Mage's Basic attack during Burst counts here. Different classes can help with the same kill, so their shares can add up to more than 100%.

How many of the team's kills its Priests helped with using their Basic abilities on the tick the enemy died. Count each enemy death once, even if several agents of this class helped. A Priest helps by giving an attacker some useful healing. Different classes can help with the same kill, so their shares can add up to more than 100%.
The average distance between living teammates on the team at the start of each tick, in map distance units. Every pair is measured once per tick, and every measurement has equal weight.
How many times agents on the team used the ability that gives this status, added together. Using it again counts once even if the status is already there. One use can give several statuses.

How often the team's agents had a Mage aura. Each agent counts once per tick, even with several auras. Both the teammate and at least one aura giver must be alive and have no spawn shield. Givers can count themselves.

How much of the team's Basic healing was more than needed. Excess healing cannot fit below maximum health after that tick's damage and healing. Priests healing the same ally share the excess in proportion to how much each healed. Does not include regeneration. Counts only Basic abilities.
How often the team saved an ally when its available Priest healing could have saved that ally from death.

How many times the team helped save allies from death. Each rescue counts once even if several teammates helped. Priest healing must keep the ally alive when that tick's damage would otherwise kill them. At least part of the helping Priest's heal must be useful. Several Priests can help; one Priest may not have enough healing to save the ally alone. Counts only help from Basic healing.

What share of the team's kills had exactly one helper. Solo kills are not always better or worse than shared kills. Only damage and useful Priest healing on the tick the enemy dies count as help. Damage on earlier ticks does not count here.

What share of the team's kills had two or more helpers. Shared kills are not always better or worse than solo kills. Only damage and useful Priest healing on the tick the enemy dies count as help. Damage on earlier ticks does not count here.

What share of the team's kills had help from a Basic ability on the tick the enemy died. Help means damaging the enemy or giving an attacker some useful healing. Count each enemy death once, even if several teammates helped. A kill can have both Basic and Ultimate help, so those shares can add up to more than 100%.

How often the team's agents had a Warrior aura. Each agent counts once per tick, even with several auras. Both the teammate and at least one aura giver must be alive and have no spawn shield. Givers can count themselves.

How much Priest healing the team provided, minus the part that was more than needed. If several Priests heal the same ally on a tick, they share the excess in proportion to how much each healed. Does not include regeneration. This healing can offset damage even if health does not rise or the ally still dies.
How much of the Basic healing the team provided was useful. This healing can offset damage even if health does not rise or the ally still dies.

Priest healing the team received, minus the healing that could not fit below maximum health after that tick's damage and healing. Does not include regeneration. This healing can offset damage even if health does not rise or the ally still dies.
How much of the Basic healing the team provided was more than needed.

What share of the team's kills its Hunters helped with using their Basic abilities on the tick the enemy died. Count each enemy death once, even if several agents of this class helped. Help must come from Basic damage. Different classes can help with the same kill, so their shares can add up to more than 100%.
Everyone's time spent dead on the team, added together. Checks who is dead at the start of each tick. Two dead teammates for one tick count as two ticks of dead time.
The average number of agents brought back by each of the team's respawn waves. Includes scheduled waves when no agent returns.

How many agents on the team at least one Mage aura covered at the start of each tick, added together. Count each teammate once per tick even with several aura givers. Both the covered agent and an aura giver must be alive and have no spawn shield. A giver can cover itself.

How many agents on the team at least one Warrior aura covered at the start of each tick, added together. Count each teammate once per tick even with several aura givers. Both the covered agent and an aura giver must be alive and have no spawn shield. A giver can cover itself.
How many times agents on the team have died, added together. Dying again after a respawn counts again.
How much of the Priest healing the team provided was useful. This healing can offset damage even if health does not rise or the ally still dies.

How much Basic Priest healing the team gave that was useful. This is Priest healing minus the part that cannot fit below maximum health after that tick's damage and healing. Priests healing the same ally share the excess in proportion to how much each healed. Does not include regeneration. Counts only Basic abilities. This healing can offset damage even if health does not rise or the ally still dies.
How much of the Priest healing the team received was useful. This healing can offset damage even if health does not rise or the ally still dies.
How much of the Priest healing the team received was more than needed.

Priest healing the team received that was useful, plus health actually restored by regeneration. Useful Priest healing and regeneration answer different questions. More regeneration may mean good disengagement or too much time away from the fight. This healing can offset damage even if health does not rise or the ally still dies.
How much of the Priest healing the team provided was more than needed. A Basic heal can still give the ally Freedom even when the ally needs none of its healing.

Help must come from Basic damage. Different classes can help with the same kill, so their shares can add up to more than 100%.

What share of the team's kills had help from an Ultimate activated on the tick the enemy died. Help means damaging the enemy or giving an attacker some useful healing. A Mage's Basic attack during Burst counts as Basic and Burst help. It does not give the Mage Ultimate kill credit. A teammate's Ultimate can still make the same kill count here.
How many times everyone on the team used their Basic abilities, added together. Using an ability again counts once even if its effect is already there. A use the game does not allow does not count.

How many times incoming damage would kill an ally and the team had enough Priest healing ready and allowed to save them. Several Priests may be needed. Each threatened ally counts once per tick. Each ally is checked separately. This does not mean the Priests could save all threatened allies at once.

How many enemies the team killed with at least two agents helping. A Priest's healing on the kill tick counts as help if it reaches an attacker and is at least partly useful. Only damage and useful Priest healing on the tick the enemy dies count as help. Damage on earlier ticks does not count here.
How much of the team's Mage damage came while Burst was already active. This shows how much the Mages relied on Burst, not how well they played.

Everyone's time with this status on the team, added together. An agent must be alive and already have the status at the start of the tick. Two affected teammates for one tick count as two. This describes agents with the status, not whoever gave it. A slow can be present without reducing movement, for example when Freedom protects the agent.

How much damage the team dealt to enemies who already had this status at the start of the tick. Includes damage beyond their remaining health. Damage that breaks an existing Trap still counts. One attack can count under several statuses.

How many times the team helped kill enemies. Each kill counts once even if several teammates helped. Help must come from Basic damage, or Basic healing that is at least partly useful to an attacker, on the tick the enemy dies. Healing another Priest who only healed does not count.

Everyone's time with this status on the team, added together. An agent must be alive and already have the status at the start of the tick. Two affected teammates for one tick count as two. This describes agents with the status, not whoever gave it.
How much Basic damage the team dealt. Counts damage after damage boosts and defenses, including damage beyond the enemy's remaining health. Counts only Basic abilities.

How often damaging teammates on the team attack the same enemy. On each tick with at least two attackers, measure the share attacking the most-shared enemy. Average those tick results. Two attackers hitting different enemies gives 0.5 (50%); both hitting one enemy gives 1 (100%). Each tick counts equally, regardless of damage dealt.
